summary: The study is scientifically sound, well‑executed, and fully archived; however prior presentation/provenance defects remain. The manuscript still embeds inline OpenAlex/archive URLs, file paths, and full hash strings and reads partly as an artifact inventory rather than conventional IEEE conference prose. These presentation issues are blocking finalisation but are correctable from the supplied artifacts.
critical_issues: Manuscript body uses inline OpenAlex/archive-style URLs and archive tokens instead of conventional numbered IEEE citations and formatted references, violating standard scholarly citation style.

Manuscript contains numerous low-level file paths, artifact filenames, and full hash strings (e.g., execution/model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA‑256 values) in the narrative, captions, and Disclosure Statement rather than a concise archival reference; this reads like an artifact inventory rather than a scientific paper.

The Disclosure Statement enumerates low-level manifest entries, file paths, and full hashes inline instead of a compact prose disclosure that cites the archived run bundle and provides only one representative manifest SHA‑256; revision required to meet track and IEEE presentation expectations.
required_revisions: Replace all inline OpenAlex/archive URLs and archive‑style in‑text links with conventional numbered IEEE citations and include properly formatted BibTeX reference entries drawn from the archived terminal_bibliographic_records. Ensure every bibliographic claim cites a numbered reference rather than an OpenAlex URL.

Remove or substantially condense inline file paths, raw artifact filenames, and full hash strings from the manuscript body, figure/table captions, and tables. Relocate the detailed provenance inventory to the archived run bundle. In Methods and the Disclosure Statement include a single concise archival citation sentence pointing to the run bundle and provide one representative manifest SHA‑256 (the preregistration SHA‑256 and/or the execution manifest representative hash), but do not list many paths or full hashes inline.

Rewrite the Disclosure Statement as compact scholarly prose that still reports required items (models used and identifiers, adapter/framework, master prompt reference, preregistration id and representative SHA‑256, high‑level execution summary such as planned/completed episode counts and model_calls_used, and a short statement that no human edited the manuscript post-lock). Remove low‑level file path and full-hash enumerations from the Disclosure Statement. Keep the Disclosure Statement fully within pages 1–5.

Edit figure and table captions to remove provenance/inventory wording and ensure concise interpretive captions suitable for IEEE two‑column formatting (no file paths, manifest names, or full hashes in captions).
optional_revisions: Add a brief methodological justification for using the paired bootstrap percentile CI given the extremely low discordance and/or include an exact alternative bound for clarity (analysis artifacts for exact alternatives are archived).
Move the explicit statement that the optional preregistration pilot was not executed earlier in Methods to improve reader flow (the fact is already present in the artifacts).

Add a short paragraph in Discussion contrasting the shared_initial estimand with estimands that permit resampling or iterative verifier‑guided regeneration and summarizing tradeoffs between repair budget and model‑call cost using archived repair_stage_count/model_calls_used values.
